chapter_theme: Under the title 'not speaking ill' (புறங்கூறாமை), the verses rebuke those who claim full knowledge without seeing the Lord, tell the heart to drop its boasting and to stop quarrelling over who is God, and praise those who contemplate him within: they see him, are loved by the knowers, and become Siva-siddhas who set aside the lesser releases.
structure_note: Only the opening verses (2512 to 2515) touch the title, as rebukes of boasting and quarrelling; 2516 to 2524 turn to contemplating the Lord within, and 2525 and 2526 define the Siva-siddhas.

2512.reading: Like men who take up a ringing, jewelled sword to strike the hare that lies in the crescent moon, the heartless who cannot see the one with the stained, jewelled throat say, 'We know it fully.'
2512.nuance: The hare is the mark on the moon, out of reach of any sword; the claim to full knowledge without sight of Siva is as idle. கறைமணி கண்டன் is Siva, his throat dark with the poison he held. நெஞ்சிலர் (without heart) may mean without feeling or without understanding.

2513.reading: As the black-legged eagle passes through the sky and the black snake leaves the dark-bottomed pool, O heart, give up your talk of your greatness; when you reach the rare, wave-tossed sea it will grow calm.
2513.nuance: The eagle's passing that makes the snake leave may stand for the Lord's coming driving off the bonds, or simply for a lesser power giving way to a greater. The last line is obscure; ஆற may mean 'to grow calm' or 'like a river'.

2514.reading: To stand at the gate of the womb and fight so that one's foes may die is petty knowledge; if it matched the great penance that the unfriendly do, the one who asked the giver would become a lone celestial.
2514.nuance: புல்லறிவாண்மை is the Kural's own chapter title, here applied to hostile striving bound to birth (கருவாயில், the womb's gate). The second half is obscure: தருவலர் கேட்ட and தனியும்பர் admit several readings, perhaps of a celestial gift-tree.

2515.reading: There is no need to quarrel: if the whole wide world agrees in thinking 'our Lord is the Lord', the eighteen hosts seek to bow and see his anklet-bound feet, and there love can be had.
2515.nuance: The verse is closest to the title: the quarrel is over whose god is God. கணம் பதினெட்டு are the eighteen classes of celestial beings. The point is that agreement, not dispute, brings even the gods to his feet.

2516.reading: If you think on the Lord who is my life more than I am, the pure one who is a great gem more than gold, the changeless one who is the life of all shining lives, he will come in the very way you think of him.
2516.nuance: The comparisons (more than myself, more than gold) rank him above what one values most. உன்னும் உறும் வகையாலே says he is reached in the form one contemplates.

2517.reading: Though many speak of the things to join with the Pure One, standing, sitting or lying, the one who conquers the five senses, quickly ends dispute and comes to know him as one becomes the one.
2517.nuance: நின்றும் இருந்தும் கிடந்தும் may be postures of practice or 'at all times'. The last line can mean that the knower becomes one with him or that such a knower is rare, only one.

2518.reading: Those who meditate on our father and Lord, who stands as subtle knowledge, as the world and as the knowledge that reckons the seven worlds, the knower of melody, are cherished by the knowers of heaven.
2518.nuance: பண் அறிவாளன் (the one who knows melody) may point to Siva as lord of music or to his knowing the songs of devotees. விண் அறிவாளர் are the celestials or the wise who know the higher world.

2519.reading: If you hold within, with eyes closed, the one whom even the celestials cannot know, and do this in the morning, with thought fixed, at all three times, your nature becomes the Parapara.
2519.nuance: முப்போதும் is the three junctures of the day, when worship is done. எண் உற வாசம் is obscure: perhaps dwelling with thought fixed, or a reckoning of breaths. The claim is that the contemplator takes the nature of the Supreme.

2520.reading: He who spread as one with the seven worlds, the lord of great grace who gave grace afterward, good within the learning of those whose minds are unsoured, is adorned with praise in a time that does not perish.
2520.nuance: கன்றா மனத்தார் (those of unsoured mind) makes goodness of heart, not learning alone, the place where he is found. பொன்றாத போது may mean 'in the time that does not end' or 'when one does not perish'.

2521.reading: I said 'Praise!' and raised my father's golden red feet on my head for ever; the ringing bell is the lamp of the inner breath, the body falls into a daze, I heard the sound and saw the hall.
2521.nuance: The bell (எறிமணி) and the inner breath's lamp are traditionally read as the inner sound and light heard and seen in yoga, and மன்று as the hall of Siva's dance within. அற்றலும் is obscure; it may be a misreading of அரற்றலும் (the outcry).

2522.reading: None who have entered within truly know Nandi, who comes before me when sought within me; I entered the nest and climbed, closed my eyes and saw his form, and I saw the seven worlds.
2522.nuance: கூடு (nest) is commonly the body, and climbing within it the yogic ascent. Seeing the seven worlds with eyes closed claims that the inner vision holds the whole.

2523.reading: To those who without flaw contemplate the fame that has come, the settled knowledge, and a little hill where honey is, he becomes the hunter who makes heaven.
2523.nuance: The small hill with honey may be an inner place (the head, where nectar is held to flow) and மறவன் (hunter) Siva as the Kirata who hunts and wins the soul. The text of lines 2 and 3 is run together and partly garbled.

2524.reading: The great ascetics whose mind became the great moon, whose pure mind is the radiant supreme bliss, entered peace that swallows the world and, their malas gone, reached rest.
2524.nuance: மாமதி plays on மதி as moon and as mind; the moon is often the cool inner light of yoga. சகம் உண (to swallow the world) is read as the world ceasing to appear. சாந்தி links this verse to the stilling of chapter 187.

2525.reading: Those who cast off the three graded releases as flawed, drive out the darkness of the bonds that had seemed pleasant, lose their pride, change 'mine' and 'I' right there and stand firm are the Siva-siddhas.
2525.nuance: பதமுத்தி மூன்றும் are the three releases short of union (dwelling in his world, nearness, his form). இதம் உற்ற (agreeable) is a sharp touch: the bonds are dark yet pleasant. எனது யான் is the pair 'mine' and 'I'.

2526.reading: The siddhas are those who have seen Siva; with excellence they are steeped in the pure and impure yet unsteeped, freed ones rooted at the root of release, powerful in that root, of the nature of Sadasiva.
2526.nuance: தோய்ந்தும் தோயாதவர் (steeped yet unsteeped) is the jivanmukta who lives among pure and impure things untouched by them. மூலம் (root) may also point to the muladhara, the root centre of yoga.

links.note: The Kural defines folly as the conceit 'we are wise'; Tirumular's heartless men say 'we know fully' while blind to the Lord, as futile as cutting the hare from the moon.

Both name the pride of 'I' and 'mine' as what must be cut. The Kural promises a world beyond the gods' to the one who cuts it; Tirumular makes cutting it, with the lesser releases set aside, the mark of the Siva-siddha.
Both make mastering the five senses the condition of reaching the Lord: the Kural's one who quenched the five senses, Tirumular's one who conquers them and knows him as one.

source_issues: The chapter title புறங்கூறாமை (not backbiting) does not fit most of the verses; only 2512 to 2515, against boasting and quarrelling, touch it loosely.
2515 line 4: வணங்ககெழு looks like a misprint for வணங்கஎழு.
2522 line 4: உலகேழுங்க்ண் டேனே is a misprint for உலகேழுங் கண்டேனே.
2523 lines 2 and 3 (சிறுவரை யொன்றுடண் / டூனமொன் றின்றி) are garbled, probably for ஒன்றுண்டு ஊனம் ஒன்றின்றி.
2526 line 2: சுத்தாசுக் தத்துடன் is a misprint for சுத்தாசுத்தத்துடன்.
